name: The Moreton Bay Fig of the Orto Botanico
species: Moreton Bay Fig (Ficus macrophylla subsp. columnaris)
age_estimate: over a century, among the garden's founding-era plantings

location.address: Orto Botanico di Cagliari, Viale Sant'Ignazio da Laconi 1, Cagliari

access: Paid entry, euro 4 (reduced/free for children under 6, over 65s, disabled visitors and school groups per italianbotanicalheritage.com). Open Monday to Saturday, closed Sundays and some public holidays.
transport: In central Cagliari; about a 15 minute walk from the Giardini Pubblici cluster (cag_001-003), roughly 700m-1.2km from the other Piazza Matteotti/Ingrao figs (cag_004, cag_005).
verify_notes: Orto Botanico di Cagliari (Università di Cagliari's botanical garden) opened 15 November 1866 under prof. Patrizio Gennari, laid out by architect Gaetano Cima in the Valle di Palabanda, on the site of a Roman amphitheatre and Punic/Roman cisterns, on about 5 hectares/12 acres. Both APGI (Associazione Parchi e Giardini Italiani) and italianbotanicalheritage.com independently name a 'monumental' Ficus macrophylla subsp. columnaris among the garden's most significant specimens. The garden's own presentation page, fetched directly (sites.unica.it/hbk/notizie-generali/presentazione/, checked 2026-09-09), states in its own words that its 'numerosi esemplari arborei notevoli... sono i più vetusti del giardino perché piantati durante la sua fase costitutiva' (its many notable tree specimens are the oldest in the garden because they were planted during its founding phase), and names this Ficus macrophylla subsp. columnaris specifically in that list alongside Phytolacca dioica and Dracaena draco. Age is therefore derived, broadly, from the garden's own founding date (1866, so up to ~160 years) allowing for the founding phase running a couple of decades past the 1866 opening, not from a bridge inferred by this pass: the source itself ties this named specimen to that period. No individual girth was found. Species and continued presence separately cross-checked against 2 iNaturalist observations of Ficus macrophylla within the garden's footprint (2005, 2019), both casual-grade but consistent. A WebSearch AI summary earlier claimed a flat '130 years old' for a Cagliari fig; that specific figure could not be confirmed on any directly-fetched page and is NOT used here, per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule; the age range above comes only from the directly-fetched hbk page. Location is garden-level only: the garden has ~37 numbered stops and colour-coded labels per taxonomic group, so an exact stop number would upgrade this to confirmed, but none of the sources fetched this pass gave one. Distinct from the already-published Ficus macrophylla trees cag_001 (Giardini Pubblici), cag_004 (Piazza Matteotti) and cag_005 (Piazza Ingrao); this is a different park (the university botanical garden) about 0.7-1.2km from that cluster, which tightens rather than widens the city's walk.

name: The Ombu of the Orto Botanico
age_estimate: over a century, among the garden's founding-era plantings

location.address: Orto Botanico di Cagliari, Viale Sant'Ignazio da Laconi 1, Cagliari

access: Paid entry, euro 4 (reduced/free for children under 6, over 65s, disabled visitors and school groups). Open Monday to Saturday, closed Sundays and some public holidays.
transport: In central Cagliari; about a 15 minute walk from the Giardini Pubblici cluster (cag_001-003).
verify_notes: A South American Phytolacca dioica (ombu / bella-ombra), an unusually broad-trunked pachycaul tree, is independently named by APGI and italianbotanicalheritage.com among the garden's monumental specimens, and sites.unica.it/hbk's own account places it along the garden's main avenue, past the bald-cypress specimens, before the Pampanini fountain. Directly fetched (sites.unica.it/hbk/notizie-generali/presentazione/, checked 2026-09-09): the page states its notable tree specimens 'sono i più vetusti del giardino perché piantati durante la sua fase costitutiva' (are the oldest in the garden, planted during its founding phase) and names Phytolacca dioica specifically in that list. Age is derived, broadly, from the garden's 1866 founding date (so up to ~160 years, allowing the founding phase to run a decade or two past the opening), because the source itself ties this named specimen to that period rather than this pass inferring a bridge. No individual girth was found this pass. Species and continued presence separately cross-checked against 3 iNaturalist observations within the garden footprint (2005, 2015, 2022), all casual-grade but from different observers/years. A WebSearch AI-generated summary earlier offered a flat '130 years old, about 9m circumference at 130cm height' for a Cagliari Phytolacca; that specific figure did not appear on any page fetched directly this pass (apgi.it, italianbotanicalheritage.com, sites.unica.it/hbk, vistanet.it were all checked and none carries it), so it is NOT used, per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule; the age range above rests only on the directly-fetched hbk page. A future pass could ask the garden directly (dip.scie.botaniche@amm.unica.it) for a documented planting date or a tape-measure girth. Location is garden-level only, same caveat as cag_011.

name: The Dragon Tree of the Orto Botanico
age_estimate: over a century, among the garden's founding-era plantings

location.address: Orto Botanico di Cagliari, near the Dipartimento di Scienze della Vita e dell'Ambiente building, Viale Sant'Ignazio da Laconi 1, Cagliari

access: Paid entry, euro 4 (reduced/free for children under 6, over 65s, disabled visitors and school groups). Open Monday to Saturday, closed Sundays and some public holidays.
transport: In central Cagliari; about a 15 minute walk from the Giardini Pubblici cluster (cag_001-003).
verify_notes: A Dracaena draco (Canary Islands dragon tree), a slow-growing, tree-form succulent whose crown grows more distinctive with age, sits near the Department of Botanical Sciences building at the top of the garden per sites.unica.it/hbk's own visitor route description ('non lontano dall'edificio del Dipartimento di Scienze Botaniche'), independently corroborated as a notable specimen by APGI. Directly fetched (sites.unica.it/hbk/notizie-generali/presentazione/, checked 2026-09-09): the page states its notable tree specimens 'sono i più vetusti del giardino perché piantati durante la sua fase costitutiva' (are the oldest in the garden, planted during its founding phase) and names Dracaena draco specifically in that list, alongside Ficus macrophylla and Phytolacca dioica (cag_011, cag_012). Age is derived, broadly, from the garden's 1866 founding date on that basis, not from the species' general reputation for longevity (which alone would be a bridge claim). No individual girth was found this pass. Species and continued presence separately cross-checked against 2 recent iNaturalist observations within the garden footprint (2020, 2025), both casual-grade. Location is garden-level only, same caveat as cag_011 and cag_012.
